newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE COCOA REVERSES TO END WITH SLIM GAINS.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE COCOA REVERSES TO END WITH SLIM GAINS.

text.p: Cocoa futures reversed earlier weaker trend to end Friday with slim gains on New York's rise but trade remained thin as players were reluctant to commit.
"The industry needs to buy and the origins need to sell but nobody is doing anything," said one trader.
The market was earlier driven lower to near imporant chart support levels and attracted some good buying support before ending the morning trade with pared losses.
The afternoon session got some encouragement from firmer New York and values finished the day with small gains.

September and volume leader December finished two stg up at 1,017 and 1,052 stg per tonne respectively. Both positions earlier came within striking distance of important support at 1,000 and 1,035 respectively.
But traders said it was difficult to see the market moving higher given the lack of short-covering interest.
"It needs shorts to provide the impetus on the upside but they are not there," the trader said.
Others say cocoa was still proned to further test on the upside based on the encouraging technical picture.

"But fundamentally, there's not much to get excited about," one trader said. Traders were keeping an eye on the U.S. CFTC Commitment of Traders report due after the close of New York trading on Friday to gauge the extent of spec long positions.
They expect the data to show net long positions of about 18,000 lots. "A figure of 15,000 or less could encourage longs to come back again," another said.
